headline: Ukraine's SkyFall has started front-line tests of StarGate, a drone built to fly wounded soldiers out of the battle zone.
score_reason: Striking machine-in-action story, but it has only just begun combat evaluation and the results are not known.
importance_line: Badly wounded soldiers who cannot be reached by ground vehicles could benefit, but the drone is only now being tested in combat and the company has shown no data on how it survives damage.
summary: The Associated Press reports, after an exclusive field demonstration, that Ukrainian defence-tech company SkyFall has handed its StarGate medical evacuation drone to a combat brigade for front-line evaluation this week. The drone has a one-way range of 15 kilometres and can carry a stretcher, but the company has shown no data on how it holds up in combat and the unit says it needs at least a month to judge it.
notes: AP text read as carried by the Sydney Morning Herald (AP original is blocked). Military story: counts toward the robot-war limit.
